conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be your doctor during this stay. You came in with abdominal pain and vomiting after an abdominal massage?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it was sudden—projectile vomiting. I’ve had this before, but it scared me this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Your vitals show a fast heart rate and slightly high blood pressure, which makes sense with pain. We’ve placed an NG tube to help decompress your stomach.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I actually placed it myself in the ER. It brought up about 250 cc. Does that mean it’s working?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s a good sign. It means we’re draining fluid and air. We’ll keep you NPO—nothing by mouth—for now and give fluids through your IV.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. But I’m worried—could this be another bowel obstruction?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s our main concern. We did a KUB X-ray, and it shows dilated bowel loops, but no clear signs of a mechanical blockage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not blocked? But why am I so bloated and in pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Given your history of Crohn’s and pseudoobstruction, this looks more like your gut isn’t moving properly—what we call an ileus or pseudoobstruction.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Like last time? I was just here a week ago.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We’re watching you closely. Surgery and GI have been consulted, and they agree with this approach.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been trying to reduce my Dilaudid at home. I don’t want to rely on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great to hear. We’ll manage your pain with IV Dilaudid and Valium, as you’ve had before, but we’ll keep it as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. I reviewed your labs. Your kidney function was a bit off on admission—creatinine was 1.2—but it’s improved to 0.9 this morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that because I was dehydrated?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, likely pre-renal. IV fluids are helping. Your hemoglobin is low at 9.3, but it’s stable—consistent with your known iron deficiency.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my white count? I’ve had low counts before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s 4.4 now—was lower last night. Hematology has seen you before and says this can happen during hospital stays and isn’t always a concern.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We got your CT scan results. No sign of small bowel obstruction. Your colon is dilated, but there’s no transition point—so likely pseudoobstruction.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about the NG tube? Is it in the right place?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s in the distal esophagus, not the stomach. We need to reposition it so it can drain better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can we do that now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the nurse will help adjust it. We’ll confirm with an X-ray.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We tried to place a PICC line yesterday for better IV access, but we couldn’t advance the wire due to vein blockages.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Because of my SVC issues?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. So we placed a midline in your left arm instead. It’s shorter but should work for fluids and meds during this stay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your latest X-ray shows the NG tube is still not quite in the stomach. The side port is at the GE junction. We may need to reposition it again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It’s frustrating. Why won’t it stay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your anatomy is complex from surgeries. We’ll keep adjusting until it’s right. The good news is your bowels are starting to decompress.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been having some diarrhea this morning—normal for me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s actually a good sign. It means your gut is starting to move again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The X-ray shows slight improvement—less distension in your colon. We’re heading in the right direction.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I try sipping water?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet. We need to see more bowel activity. We’ll try an enema today to help stimulate movement.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great news—you passed stool after the enema yesterday. That’s a big step forward.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel a bit better. Can we remove the NG tube?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll check an X-ray first. If your stomach stays decompressed, we can consider removing it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The X-ray shows the NG tube is now in the stomach. But since you’re improving, we’re going to try removing it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I hate having it in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done well overnight—no nausea or vomiting. We’re going to start you on clear liquids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I have broth?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll start with broth and see how you tolerate it. Small sips at first.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve kept down clear liquids. Today, we’ll advance you to a soft diet—mashed potatoes, applesauce, things like that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m really hungry. Can I have more?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We have to be cautious. Your gut is still recovering. Let’s see how you do today, then maybe more tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve tolerated the soft diet well. No vomiting. Your labs are stable. We’re making good progress.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: When can I go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If you keep this up, likely in a few days. We want to make sure you can eat and keep food down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your blood cultures came back negative—no infection. That’s reassuring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I had a low-grade fever the other night. Was that just from stress?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. Your chest X-ray showed a chronic opacity in your right lung, but no new pneumonia. It’s likely stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The NG tube was replaced yesterday because it got dislodged, but we’ve removed it again today since you’re doing so well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I didn’t even notice. I feel so much better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve been on a regular diet since yesterday—how’s your stomach feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. No pain, no vomiting. Just mild bloating, but that’s normal for me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s excellent. We’ll plan for discharge tomorrow if all goes well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve made it through the night with no issues. We’ll get your discharge papers ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No changes to my meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No changes. You’ll continue your usual medications, including Flagyl as you’ve restarted.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if this happens again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If you have severe pain, vomiting, or can’t keep liquids down, come back to the ER. Otherwise, follow up with your GI doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’m really glad to be going home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You did great. Take it easy, stick to soft foods for a few days, and call if anything worries you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your discharge orders are in. You’re cleared to go home this morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel so much better. Thank you for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Remember—follow up with your PCP and GI team. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just checking in before you leave. Any last questions?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I think I’m good. I’ll follow the instructions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’ll see you in clinic if needed. Safe travels home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m all packed. Just waiting on the ride.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. I’ll sign your discharge papers. You’re officially going home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you again. I really appreciate it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. Call us if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m heading out now. Bye!

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Bye! Feel better soon.
